newsitem.title: USA: U.S. school will not expel girl over lunch knife.
newsitem.headline: U.S. school will not expel girl over lunch knife.

text.p: An 11-year-old honour student, suspended for bringing a steak knife to school with her lunch, will not be expelled despite tough new rules on weapons, officials said on Friday.

Charlotte Kirk was suspended from class and then arrested on Oct. 18 for violating a policy that gives Columbia, South Carolina, principals no choice but to suspend all students caught with weapons on school grounds.
She could have been expelled, but a hearing officer decided late on Friday afternoon to let the girl, who has never been in trouble before, return to school.

Sheila Johnson Chaney, a school spokeswoman, said the policy was enacted 11 months ago to stop violence in the schools. Already this year, 30 students have been expelled for having weapons, three of them at Hopkins Middle School, which Kirk attends.

"It may seem harsh, looking at it in the cold light of day, but it's for the greater good of the students and to protect their interests. Students should not have to fear anything at school, except maybe a bad grade when they do not do their homework," Chaney said.
A week ago, Kirk packed a lunch of leftover baked chicken, black-eyed peas and an apple. She threw in a serrated steak knife to cut the chicken with.
At lunch, a friend saw the knife and told Kirk she had better ask a teacher if it was all right to use it.
The teacher reported the incident to the principal, who called police.
"It's always a tough thing to call, but a principal is not given any prerogative," Chaney said.
Columbia residents jumped to Kirk's defence. Chaney said more than 100 people had called the school to complain after a local newspaper reported the incident.
A growing number of schools across the country have adopted similar policies to reduce school violence.
Chaney said school officials did not question Kirk's assertion that she planned to use the knife as a utensil, not a weapon.

"But what if someone had taken it out of her lunch box and threatened someone with it?" Chaney asked. "Across the country we've seen examples of well-behaved honour students who have gone over the edge."
